Option B: Pain during closing and opening of mouth
Option D: Musculoskeletally stable position of condyle in the fossae
Explanation:
'D' [Okeson 3rd ed 263]

Musculoskeletally stable position of condyle in the fossae means centric relation (CR). Various CR registration techniques were developed to manage the many clinical contingencies that obstruct capturing a repeatable CR registration record. Some of them are Roth power centric bite, Tongue tip to soft palate, Chin point guidance, bimanual manipulation, and Leaf gauge.

Leaf Gauge Technique:
• To obtain an interocclusal record, a soft plastic leaf gauge should be placed between the subject's maxillary and mandibular incisors such that the number of leaves provide sufficient vertical dimension to just disocclude the posterior teeth. This should be maintained for 5 minutes with subjects sitting upright.
• The subject should be placed in a supine position, the leaf gauge is removed without allowing any occlusal contact, and the PVS registration material should be applied to the occlusal surfaces of the mandibular teeth. The leaf gauge should be replaced and the subject instructed to close into the registration material in the previous position, using the leaf gauge as an anterior stop. The registration material allowed to set and then removed from the patient's mouth.
• The concept behind the leaf gauge is that when only the anterior teeth occlude, the directional force provided by the elevator muscles seats the condyles in a superoanterior position within the fossae. A leafgauge must be used carefully so the condyles will not be deflected away from the CR.

Explanation:

Centric relation (CR) is the most controversial concept in dentistry. Most of the controversies are pertaining to the position of the head of the condyle in the glenoid fossa during centric relation position. This ranges from a retruded posterior position, to superior position and then to an anterior superior position.
For almost the last six decades we assumed CR to be the most retruded position of the heads of the condyles in the glenoid fossae. Recently we could come to a conclusion that it is not the most retruded position of the heads of the condyles but rather the most anterior and superior position.

If articulating paper is used in the mouth to locate deflective occlusal contacts, shifting of the denture bases, tissue distortions or eccentric closures by the patients, as well as the presence of saliva, can prevent the articulating paper marks from accurately recording errors.

• OO = Plane of orientation of the occlusal plane

Subject: Complete Denture
Question: Transfer of hinge opening axis is compulsory in:
Explanation:
'D' [Nallaswamy 1st ed 535 / Winkler 2nd ed 185]

Hinge axis is an imaginary line passing through the centre of the condyles when the mandible rotates in the sagittal plane. The axis of rotation which coincides with the CR position of the mandible is called true hinge axis.
Patient's hinge axis can be transferred into the articulator (semiadjustable or fully adjustable) with the help of face bow.
A face bow transfer is essential when cusp teeth are used and also to change the occlusal vertical dimensions.
Arbitrary mounting of maxillary casts without a face bow transfer can introduce errors in occlusion of prosthesis. So transferring the hinge axis is must when we are planning for full mouth rehabilitation and in patients who require increase in vertical dimension.

Subject: Complete Denture
Question: Movement of denture base was the least in patient with poor ridges when
Explanation:
'C' [Nallaswamy 1st ed 10 / Winkler 2nd ed 237, 238]

Cuspless teeth also called as non-anatomical teeth or monoplane teeth. In cases with the highly resorbed ridges, cuspless teeth are preferred as they do not get locked and displace the dentures during lateral movements. During function, the monoplane teeth eliminate inclined plane forces which create displacement of the denture base.

Subject: Complete Denture
Question: Most commonly affected word if maxillary incisor teeth are anteriorly placed?
Explanation:
'D' [Zarb & Bolender 12th ed 383-4]

Linguoalveolar sounds for eg: S, Z, Sh, and J are made by contact of lip of the tongue with the most anterior part of palate or lingual side of anterior teeth. When the patient pronounces the words starting with S, the upper and lower incisors should approach end to end but not touch. If the upper anterior teeth are placed most anteriorly, it is difficult to pronounce the linguoalveolar sounds like S, G, Sh, J.
The labiodental sounds F & V are made between the upper incisors and the labiolingual centre to the posterior third of lower lip. If the upper anterior teeth are too short (set too high up) the V sound will be more like an F. if they are too long (set too far down) the F will sound more like V.

Subject: Complete Denture
Question: In India during summers teeth arrangement for occlusion check-up is done in:
Explanation:
'C' [Philips 11th ed 284, 292]

Base plate waxes used principally to establish the initial arch form in the construction of complete dentures. It has 3 types. Type I, II, III depending upon the flow at given temperatures.
• Type I: a soft wax used for building veneers
• Type II: a medium wax is designed for patterns to be tried in the mouth in the normal climatic conditions
• Type III: a hard wax for trial fitting in the mouth in tropical climates
Corrective wax is used to make a type of dental impression.
